# Wiki sync status

Which pages still need copying into the live Wiki. See [`README.md`](./README.md) for how the
mirror works.

**You do not edit this file.** Open it whenever you have time, paste the pages the table names,
then tell Claude which ones you did - the table clears itself and the pages are stamped as synced.

The table below is **maintained automatically** by
[`.claude/hooks/wiki-sync-status.sh`](../../.claude/hooks/wiki-sync-status.sh), which re-checks
every page against [`.claude/wiki-synced.tsv`](../../.claude/wiki-synced.tsv) at the end of every
turn. It cannot go stale, so it does not need double-checking before you act on it. The prose under
it, describing *what* changed in each page, is written by Claude.

## What changed in each page

Five separate features are sitting in these six pages, not one. Each is described here so you know
what you are pasting and why the page moved.

### The worklog **currency** setting

Configuration gained a "Currency used for worklog costs" drop-down (country + ISO code, defaulting
to United States (USD)), and every cost the app shows now carries that code - entry cards, the
summary strip, the worklog editor, the "Cost (DKK)" input label, and the exported PDF/ZIP.

- **`Configuration-tab`** - the Workbooks section gained the new drop-down, with a note that
  several countries share a currency and that nothing is converted.
- **`Workbooks-Daily-use`** - the Work done paragraph said "the application never asks about
  currency, so use whatever you bill in", which is now the opposite of what the app does.
- **`Workbooks-Browsing-and-search`** - the summary paragraph said "There is no currency symbol -
  it is your own number back again", same problem.

### Time is shown as hours and minutes

Decimal `2.0 h` became `2 hours` / `1 hour and 15 minutes` everywhere the app displays a time. The
Time spent *input* is the one exception and still takes decimal hours, reading back underneath in
hours and minutes as you type.

- **`Workbooks-Daily-use`** - the Work done paragraph, plus a new note that the input is the only
  decimal field.
- **`Workbooks-Browsing-and-search`** - the ASCII layout diagrams and the totals paragraph.
- **`Workbooks-Getting-started`** - the one-line Work done bullet.

### Zero values are omitted rather than shown

A worklog with no cost or no time simply leaves that figure out, so a plain note reads `1 comment`
instead of `0 h · 0 USD · 1 comment · 0 links · 0 photos · 0 files`. The *expanded* breakdown
deliberately keeps its zeroes.

- **`Workbooks-Browsing-and-search`** - both the worklog-list and summary-strip paragraphs.

### The workbook storage layout changed - **breaking, with no migration**

Workbooks are now `workbook_{id}/` folders, each worklog a folder holding its own `index.json`
together with its attachments; `entryCount`/`lastEntryId` became `worklogCount`/`lastWorklogId`.

**Older workbooks are not converted and will not appear.** This is the one change here with a real
consequence for existing users, so it is worth reading the wording before it goes live.

- **`Workbooks-Export-and-data`** - the folder-layout tree, plus an upgrade warning blockquote.

### Workbooks record an end date

A Closed workbook shows "ended" on the day its last outstanding worklog was closed; the start date
never changes. Workbooks closed by an older version have no end date and keep showing their start
date.

- **`Workbooks-tab`** - three paragraphs under the Open/Closed section.

### Smaller behaviour changes

All in **`Workbooks-Daily-use`** and **`Workbooks-Browsing-and-search`**:

- Schematic previews can be dragged to reorder, and the order is saved per workbook.
- The search filter now survives a board change, and is cleared with the ✕ in the box.
- Search highlighting follows you into the worklog editor.
- A new worklog with unsaved content asks for confirmation before closing.
- An oscilloscope capture filed into a worklog is **moved**, not copied.
- "Cancel entry" in the bar is now "Cancel", and `Esc` also works.

## How this file maintains itself

The table at the top is rewritten at the end of every turn by
[`.claude/hooks/wiki-sync-status.sh`](../../.claude/hooks/wiki-sync-status.sh), which compares each
page against the blob hash recorded in
[`.claude/wiki-synced.tsv`](../../.claude/wiki-synced.tsv). A page appears there whenever its
current bytes differ from the bytes last pasted.

**It compares content, not commits**, deliberately: pages are normally pasted while their edits are
still uncommitted, and a commit-based check reports every page as permanently stale in that state.

When you have pasted some pages, just say so - "pasted Configuration-tab and Workbooks-tab", or
"pasted all of them". They are stamped at their current content and drop off the table. Behind the
scenes that runs
[`.claude/hooks/wiki-mark-synced.sh`](../../.claude/hooks/wiki-mark-synced.sh), which you can also
run yourself.

The hook maintains the **table** only. This prose is written by Claude, because whether a change is
user-visible and how to describe it is a judgement a script cannot make.
